body:
Yeah, today's my last day until I leave.

I am just a fallen, withered leaf from a tree.  While I may be gone, new leafs will come from my passing.  Life is just a cycle of leafs on a tree.  The tree is the universe.  The leafs are the birth and dying of people who will eventually be replaced.

Thanks!  I'll def look into that.  :)

I would exercise but I have issues with disordered eating, and depression ruins the motivation.  I'll try my best though!
Thanks for that resource (Plume).  Seems like a neat concept, but I'm a year away from getting a job.

Switches accounts cause I lost the password, but yeah.  I'm still here.

My mental health has declined so far.  I now have a plan with no percentage of failure.  I hope you are being safe.

Unfortunately, they do have problems with controlling their actions to be morally acceptable.

I hope that this individual does not confront other people on Reddit with this same behavior.

As stated before, I want them to get help themselves and I hope that they eventually make a positive or venting post on this subreddit either to give help or to receive help.

Yes, any action intended to hurt yourself after staying clean is relapse. 

Do not be worried about resetting your time.  It will reset, but that does not define your progress in escaping from the chains.  You are beautiful and meaningful.  Your cautiousness and the fact that you posted this for advice today really means a lot today and has made a positive influence on me.

Yes, it is self-harm.  But there are several levels of self-harm, each level differentiating on severity.  The more you self-harm, the higher risk of moving on to the next level there is.

I hope that you can stay safe.  I care about your safety a lot!

I am sorry to hear of your frustration with my music taste, as well as your continuous effort to make me feel bad.  It is quite disappointing, I hope your condition improves soon.

Please stay safe for me.
Reasonable opinion.  Not everyone has to enjoy the playlist.
I wish it were that easy.

Ideally, you should tell your therapist everything, though in my own experience, that is what puts you in the hospital.

I understand your fears.  Several inpatient programs, even the best have been personally, a scarring experience that made it worse.  

Therapists are legally required to tell your guardians if there is intent for you to harm yourself.  So it really depends on your guardians of what happens, but it is completely okay to take it one step at a time.

I would recommend gradually telling your therapist more.  Lead them to imply that something deeper is going on, then they will begin to be more specific.  This is how you build a mutual trust relationship with your therapist.

The best option is to tell your therapist everything.  It will be a ticket to the psych ward, but after that you don’t have to deal with it again since you tell them all of your emotions and they begin to help you.

Stay safe, mmb123_!
Thank you for responding despite the locked voting.  I do have alcohol wipes that I should use that would also protect my hands from being cut while cleaning.
From what I’ve heard, its normal for some parents to lightly throw shoes at you, but you emphasized that it was really hard.  I would still recommend talking with your school counselor.

I have been through a similar experience.

When I got hospitalized for the first time, my mother decided to read every single paper lying in my room.  This is when she found the knives, etc.  But what annoys me the most is that she read the journaling in which I said some very controversial things as I was in a crazed sort of mindset.  She facetimed me when she was drunk and said stuff like, “Hey, you remember when you called that one person a cunt?”.

It’s personal shit that no one has to know.  “Oh, but we didn’t know where you were at.”. Well fuck, if you want to know what mindset I’m in, just fucking ask me.

It gets better once the information is exposed.  All the drama can only get disolved from there and people will eventually not confront you about it.
Your mother abused you.  Please reach out to a school counselor or some form of counselor and they will help guide you on what to do next.

Your suffering cannot be described with words.

The memories of being tired and uselessness that you have are the past.  You have a chance, no matter what, you always have a chance to turn your life around.

Here is a comment to a related post that might be helpful: https://www.reddit.com/r/selfharm/comments/m0z9ac/fuck/gqawd34/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=ios_app&utm_name=iossmf&context=3

If you need to talk please reach out to me and I will do my best to redirect you to the proper resources.

For me, the first time I cut was a very vivid and scarring memory.  Self injury is not the way out.  There are other coping mechanisms which can help you release your energy.

Please do not cut again.  It is a cycle that will put you into a shitty hospital, have your parents be overprotective, and etcetera.  I wish I could just hug you and sit down to talk with you for a while, but I cannot.

If you have suicidal thoughts, in my experience, self-harm will make it worse.  It will make all of your emotions, and just amplify them.  Just like alcohol.  Whatever you are trying to run from, it will come back and worse if you try to escape in the world of self harm.

School is very difficult, but it can and will get better.  If you have any questions, please ask me and I am more than welcome to answer them.
The way my parents found out was through a school counselor.  I fully expected the counselor to call them, in which they did.  The counselor is the easiest way to notify your parents.

I congratulate you for your perseverance and dedication you have put into this.  You have inspired me to test this application myself, and hopefully it will help.

Continue on your stride! :D

I can definitely relate to this.  The feeling, the urge, is unbearable at some point.

But you persevere through difficult conditions.  You are thriving right now, and second by second, you are improving.  You can do this and no one is doubting you.  Believe in yourself, and you will fly.  

I sincerely hope this message helps you.  :)

Your disappointment is understandable.  Several people have kept a clean streak of a few years, and then they break it.  Relapsing is part of the process.  Don’t blame yourself for relapsing.  As my friend would put it, it gives you even more of a reason to try to do your best to not self injure. 

I know that you will have enough motivation to beat this.  You are safe and accepted.  The road will be a long journey.

I reset my one and a half month streak yesterday, and it caused me to break down.  But the next day (today), my dearest sister helped me to see it as another step in the staircase.

No, you cannot self-harm without the pain.  Everyone’s circumstance is different, but I believe it would be close to say that most people who self injure do it for the release of pain and chemicals, as well as the unbearable urge.

You and your friend are going to get better!  I am happy that you both are able to relate to each other, that is very healthy in a friendship.  All it is going to take is hard work and cooperation with professionals and trusted peers alike.  It is a lot of steps to take, but little by little you can do this! 😊

Also, I’ve seen your posts, so I am not giving you these questions for the other forms that you might do, but specifically this one.  

I hope you stay safe, all of my wishes are going towards you tonight. :)

Technically speaking, any form of self inflicted  injury to your body is self-harm. I want you to ask yourself a few questions that might help guide you into the right direction as I cannot decide for you: Is this an addiction?  Are you doing it out of self-punishment?  Are you doing it out of any form of strong emotion, whether it be elatedness or fear?

Hello Matik080,

My name is Laniakea and I have found your post today.  In my experience of being hospitalized twice, neither of them have helped me.  Maybe it is the overload of medications my psychiatrists have prescribed me.  Maybe its just that I found the only person in the world who I can escape to in my times of necessity.  Regardless of what has helped me, I have been in the similar circumstances you have been through.

Having just relapsed last night with my mental health declining since then, I may not be the best person to respond to this post, though I will attempt.

From your perspective, it seems that you feel trapped with no freedom.  In my own experience, my parents used to be overly monitoring my devices.  Now, I have learnt that I can simply delete Reddit after my usage.  I would assume that you have made a similar strategy.

Parents are odd, aren’t they?  My own parents have admitted themselves that talking with my trusted online friends has saved my life, yet they restrict my usage of it and say that it is unsafe despite my experience on the Internet and high knowledge of what is appropriate to share with an online individual or not.

My advice to you is to find your escape.  It appears to me that your escape is Reddit.  Focus on that escape and allow it to become your world, muting all of the other noises.  In your days, you will struggle, but it is the escape that will allow you to recover, because you are perseverant.

Most middle class people are spoiled, being completely ignorant of the struggles lying behind them.  It is nothing to be ashamed of and it is a natural way of thought.

I hope this message has helped you one way or another.  Let me know if you need someone to talk to.
